title: Cascade Analytics - Private VPC Discovery
summary: High-level discovery about Cascade's requirements for a private Redwood deployment in their AWS accounts. Key constraints: EU data residency for some customers, strict KMS controls, no internet-facing endpoints, prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink, need SOC2 artifacts and runtime audit logs. SE to follow up with network diagram and benchmark plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We also have Priya from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Ethan: Good, thanks. Ethan here. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:12] Priya: Hi Ethan, Sofia, Avery, thanks — I'll do the technical run-through, Jordan will handle procurement/questions.
[00:20] Sofia: Quick heads up — we put together a list of requirements in the invite: data residency (EU), no public endpoints, keys must live in our KMS, and we need audit logs forwarded to Splunk.
[00:32] Jordan: Great — that's exactly what we wanted to confirm. Can you walk through your current infra?
[00:40] Liam: We're on AWS, most stuff in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. We run EKS + some EC2. We have a strict VPC design — no inbound internet traffic allowed to compute subnets.
[00:48] Priya: Understood. For Redwood Private we can deploy a private control plane inside your VPC or allow our control plane in a customer-managed VPC? (mmm slight garble) Sorry, what I mean is we offer Private with a private control plane that can sit in your account, or a customer-managed VPC with peering/private endpoints.
[01:05] Sofia: We definitely want the control plane in our account. Our security team won't allow any shared control plane that routes through public internet.
[01:10] Avery: And all keys must be in our KMS; if there's any HSM requirement we need to know.
[01:15] Priya: We support KMS integration — you can bring your CMK. For HSM-backed keys we have options, but we'll need to map what operations require the HSM.
[01:25] Jordan: Could you describe the expected workload? QPS, sequence lengths, latency SLOs?
[01:32] Ethan: We're primarily generating personalized marketing copy and some customer support summarization. Burst-y traffic, peaks around 200 rps for short requests (averages 80 tokens). Latency target: p95 under 600ms if possible; cost sensitivity is important though.
[01:45] Priya: 600ms p95 is aggressive for private with strict isolation but doable with Dedicated GPU pools pinned to the region. We'll want to control batching and KV cache to meet latency.
[01:55] Sofia: On network: do you require VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or can we use AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints?
[02:02] Priya: We support both patterns. Typical pattern for customers who disallow cross-account peering is PrivateLink endpoints with interface ENIs in the customer's subnet — that avoids peering but requires endpoint services configuration on our side. For customer-managed deployments we can also deploy into your VPC and avoid any peering.
[02:18] Liam: If you deploy into our VPC, what's the communication footprint? E.g., do you need internet egress for model downloads or usage metrics?
[02:26] Priya: If we deploy private (customer VPC), we still need some optional egress for updates and telemetry unless you host an internal mirror. We can disable telemetry egress and provide offline update mechanisms, but that adds ops overhead. We'll list specifics in a network diagram.
[02:40] Jordan: Also regulatory: you mentioned EU residency — does this need to be enforced at the inference runtime level or just storage?
[02:48] Sofia: Both. Logs and token-level data must stay in EU. Any fallback to US endpoints is a hard no.
[02:54] Priya: We can run the full stack in eu-west-1 / eu-central-1. For failover we can restrict to EU-only regions. We'll ensure model variants and fallback routing stay in EU.
[03:06] Avery: Auditability — we need immutable audit logs with user identities, model versions, and request metadata shipped to our SIEM. Also RBAC — who can call what model.
[03:16] Priya: We emit detailed request logs, model versions, and per-token billing metadata. For SSO we integrate SAML/Okta and support fine-grained RBAC policies. We can also push logs to your S3 or Splunk.
[03:27] Ethan: Great. On performance — we want to run your recommended benchmark. We have a sample workload and a set of test prompts. Could Redwood run a benchmark in our account?
[03:36] Priya: Yes, we offer a 2-4 week pilot where we'll spin up a dedicated pool in your VPC and run benchmarks. We'll need an IAM role with limited permissions and a VPC subnet for the instances.
[03:45] Liam: For peering vs PrivateLink: PrivateLink is preferred by our network team because peering is disallowed across org boundaries. If you require peering we'll need a formal security review.
[03:55] Jordan: Noted. We can set up PrivateLink. There are some performance tradeoffs but if we put the endpoints in the same AZ and configure ENI scaling it's usually fine.
[04:06] Priya: One caveat — PrivateLink adds extra hop and NAT implications for TLS termination; for low-latency SLOs we recommend colocating inference workers in customer's VPC (i.e., customer-managed deployment) if they need sub-600ms p95.
[04:20] Ethan: So options summary: hosted (fast to spin up, not acceptable for our EU-only requirement), dedicated (Redwood-managed but reserved capacity — maybe ok?), private/customer VPC (control plane and compute in our account) — which is most realistic for us?
[04:33] Priya: For strict isolation and data residency, customer VPC private deployment is the best fit. Dedicated (Redwood-managed) can be done in EU but still involves cross-account networking unless we deploy in your account.
[04:45] Sofia: We also need to understand the upgrade/patch process: how do you do model updates, kernel patches, and how do we certify them?
[04:53] Priya: We run staged rollouts: canary -> gradual -> full. For private installs we can coordinate with you; we can hold updates until you run your acceptance tests. We'll provide changelogs and the exact binary artifacts so you can scan them.
[05:06] Avery: Is there support for bringing your own model weights? We have internal models we might want to host.
[05:12] Priya: BYO models is supported in Private deployments, though we'd validate compatibility and optimize quantization. Licensing and IP controls would be included in the PO.
[05:20] Jordan: On pricing, I'll follow up with modelled pricing for the pilot (monthly reserved nodes for the pilot window) and incremental per-token charges if applicable.
[05:28] Ethan: For the pilot we'd like an estimate: 2 dedicated GPUs, run-for 2 weeks, synthetic peak at 200 rps.
[05:35] Priya: We'll draft a benchmark plan and cost estimate. We'll also need a network diagram from you showing subnets and route tables.
[05:42] Sofia: One more: encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for internal service-to-service traffic? Our security policy requires mTLS between services inside VPC.
[05:51] Priya: Yes, we support mTLS. We'll also propose mutual TLS for PrivateLink endpoints and provide cert rotation docs.
[06:00] Liam: Anything else about logging retention? We keep logs for 7 years for compliance, but maybe you hold shorter.
[06:07] Priya: We can configure retention on the log shipping side. By default Redwood retains request logs for 90 days in hosted but for Private you'll control long-term retention in your S3.
[06:15] Jordan: Ok let's surface next steps. We'll compile security docs and a pilot plan. Priya will send the network diagram template and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:25] Ethan: Sounds good. Can we also get SOC2/ISO certificates and data processing addendum?
[06:30] Jordan: Yes — I'll share SOC2 attestation, DPIA template, and DPA.
[06:35] Avery: We'll schedule a technical deep dive with our network and security folks; ideally next week.
[06:40] Priya: That works — I'll bring our network architect.
[06:44] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with dates and docs.
[06:48] Sofia: Thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription artifacts (KV cache spelled K V cash or 'K V cash' in some places), minor speaker label swap around 02:00 where Jordan and Priya overlap.
